videos.headline: The Suez Canal Short has 14 views after 2 days, while the channel's next two Shorts passed 685 and 1,207 in about a day.

why.text: 14 views by the live count at 2.1 days; Greenland has 1,207 and the Sahara 685 at 1.5 days or less.
Analytics has no views for it yet, so no % viewed or drop points; the verdict is on views alone.
At 60 s it is twice as long as a typical Short, and its title is a 'what if' rather than the 'Why?' map question the two that took off asked.

videos.next: Stay with a place you can point to on the map and ask why it is the way it is, like the Greenland and Sahara Shorts.

videos.headline: Greenland is the channel's best Short so far: 1,213 views, and viewers watched it more than once on average.

why.text: 1,213 views, the most of the channel's 7 Shorts (the others 0 to 955).
110% viewed and 63.4% stayed to watch on 476 Analytics views; 44.2% held after the hook.
US viewers were 83% of views and watched 160% of it; viewers in the Philippines (12%) watched 32%.
The biggest fall was 15.2 points at 5.9 s; the line isn't known because the stats job looked for this channel's timeline in the wrong folder (fixed tonight).

videos.next: Make more 'why does this place belong to that country' Shorts about a well-known place with a surprising owner, the form that got 1,213 views.

videos.headline: The green-Sahara Short has 925 views in about two days and 22 likes, the channel's second best start; Analytics has no data on it yet.

why.text: 925 views 2.1 days after publishing, against 14 for the Suez Canal Short at the same age; only Greenland (1,213) has more.
22 likes, the most of any of the channel's Shorts; 0 Analytics views so far, so no % viewed or drop points yet.

videos.next: Pair a well-known place with a fact that flips how it looks today (green Sahara, Danish Greenland): both such 'Why?' titles passed 900 views.

videos.headline: The hidden Welsh power station Short reached 164 views, under a third of the channel's median, and lost most viewers in the first cave line.

why.text: 164 views at about 48 hours, against the channel's median of 569.
74.4% stayed to watch, above the median of 61%, but only 8.8% held after the hook (median 15.7%) across its 61 s.
The steepest fall, 31.2 points, came at 6.4 s on 'Under the grass of Elidir Fawr, in Snowdonia, there is a cave 51 m high…'.

videos.next: Answer the hook's 'why hide it' in the second line instead of a list of Welsh place names: the long cave line is where 31 points left.

videos.headline: The one-passport-for-every-country Short has 1,040 views and 21 likes in two days, but Analytics has no data on it yet.

why.text: 1,040 public views 2.1 days after publishing, against the channel's median of 569 at 48 hours.
21 likes, the most on the channel's recent Shorts; Analytics has 0 views so far, so no drop points yet.

videos.next: Make another 'what if one rule applied to every country' challenge Short, and check its drop points once Analytics catches up.

videos.headline: The Tristan da Cunha Short pulled 1,197 views in two days, above the channel's median, but fewer viewers stayed than usual and a fifth left on the distances line.

why.text: 1,197 views at about 48 hours, against the channel's median of 814 (6 Shorts).
46.8% stayed to watch, under the channel's median of 59.7%; 49.4% viewed against a median of 60.5%.
The steepest fall, 20.2 points, came at 6.0 s on 'Its nearest neighbour, Saint Helena, sits 2,430 km to the north, and South Africa is 2,816 km away to the east.'
14.1% held after the hook across its 71 s, against a median of 21.1%.

videos.next: Give the island's remoteness in one picture and one number (the nearest neighbour only) instead of two distances in one line: that line is where 20 points left.

videos.headline: The Hormuz-shuts-for-a-week Short has 1,217 views and 18 likes in two days, but Analytics has no data on it yet.

why.text: 1,217 public views 2.1 days after publishing, against the channel's median of 814 at 48 hours.
Analytics has 0 views for it so far, so there is no stayed-to-watch figure or drop point yet.

videos.next: Make another 'one chokepoint closes, who runs out first' challenge Short, and check its drop points once Analytics catches up.

videos.headline: The English-cities Short reached more people than most (1,378 views) but kept fewer of them: half had left before the reason was given.

why.text: 1,378 views so far against the channel's median of 1,060 (7 earlier Shorts); 96.7% came from the Shorts feed.
55.3% viewed and 48.9% stayed to watch, against medians of 61.2% and 59.8%; 16.1% held after the hook against 22.8%.
The steepest fall, 19.1 points, came at 5.4 s on 'From London to the mill towns of the north, it happens again and again', the second beat, which restates the pattern instead of showing the reason.

videos.next: Show the first piece of the answer (the wind blowing smoke east) in the second beat instead of a second example of the pattern.

videos.headline: The Antarctica Short drew 1,023 views and 20 likes, close to the channel's median; its watch data hasn't arrived yet.

why.text: 1,023 views so far against the channel's median of 1,060 (7 earlier Shorts).
No Analytics rows yet (0 Analytics views), so % viewed and where viewers left are not known.

videos.next: Too little data for a change: judge its challenge hook once its watch data lands.

videos.headline: Russia and the Urals beat the channel's median on both views and % viewed.

why.text: 1,099 views in 48 hours against the Shorts median of 889.
66.2% viewed against the median of 61.2%; 60.3% stayed to watch.
The steepest fall, 12.9 points at 6.4 s, came on the Siberia description line, the second beat again.
95.5% of views came from the Shorts feed; CTR 7.1%.

videos.next: Make the second beat a turn, not a description: Yermak's crossing could have come at 6 s instead of a line about the forest.

videos.headline: Malacca held viewers best of the channel's recent Shorts: 80.7% viewed.

why.text: 1,031 views in 48 hours against the median of 889.
80.7% viewed against the median of 61.2%; 62.1% stayed to watch.
13.6 points left at 5.7 s on "It's only a thought experiment, but look how thin this lane is".

videos.next: Keep the what-if hook, but drop the "only a thought experiment" aside from the second beat and open straight on the 2.8 km lane.

videos.headline: Lesotho kept viewers as well as usual but reached few: 160 views.

why.text: 160 views so far against the Shorts median of 889 in 48 hours.
61.3% viewed, on the median of 61.2%; 60.2% stayed to watch.
The biggest fall, 16.9 points at 8.1 s, came on the size line ("30,355 km², about as big as Belgium").

videos.next: The feed didn't push it: test a title that names the country inside (Lesotho) as the surprise, and keep size comparisons out of the first 10 s.

videos.headline: Panama's canal held viewers (90.6% viewed) but only 185 people saw it.

why.text: 185 views against the Shorts median of 735 in 48 hours.
90.6% viewed against the median 61.1%, and held after the hook 40.6%.
Stayed to watch 49.4% against the median 59.4%: half swiped away in the first seconds.
Its falls are small (at most 9.1 points, at 1.5 s and 9.9 s).

videos.next: Its body works; the first second loses the feed. Open on the empty lock, not the question.

videos.headline: Australia's dingo fence kept viewers well (67.8% viewed) but lost the most of them on the second beat.

why.text: 67.8% viewed against the Shorts median of 61.1%.
1,130 views against the 48-hour median of 735; 97.3% of views came from the Shorts feed.
Stayed to watch 48.8% against the median 59.4%, and held after the hook only 22.9%.
The steepest fall, 13.9 points at 5.7 s, is on the cliffs line "on the cliffs of the south coast": the second beat again.

videos.next: Make the second beat show the fence's payoff (sheep on one side, dingoes on the other) instead of where the fence starts.
